disagreements.docsSay: `allowed-tools` pre-approves the listed tools for the turn; it “does not restrict which tools are available: every tool remains callable”. `disallowed-tools` or a deny rule removes tools.
disagreements.agrees: dnacenta §3.2 (“Tools pre-approved while this skill is active”)

disagreements.says: MCP scoping is two-way: project (`.mcp.json`) and user (`~/.claude.json`)
disagreements.docsSay: Three scopes. The default for `claude mcp add` is LOCAL: private to you, per project, also stored in `~/.claude.json`. Same-name precedence is local, then project, then user; the whole entry is used, nothing is merged.
disagreements.agrees: dnacenta §2.4 lists local, project, user and managed

disagreements.says: `argument-hint`: “asks for an argument when invoked without parameters”
disagreements.docsSay: A hint “shown during autocomplete”. It does not prompt or validate. If no placeholder in the body uses an argument, Claude Code appends `ARGUMENTS: <value>` to the skill.

disagreements.says: Use `allowed-tools` “to restrict tool access during skill execution”
disagreements.docsSay: The docs are more precise (pre-approval, not restriction). Project rule: the guide decides what is examinable, the docs decide technical facts, so the question tests the docs' behaviour and the explanation says where the wording differs.
